page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor running at 2.55 GHz. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps.

Benchmark results show strong performance in single-core CPU execution via stress-ng and high memory efficiency in PassMark memory tests. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth for large, potentially uncached blocks fall into the lower percentiles. Text generation using small language models demonstrates strong throughput, while database operations, static web serving, and software compilation align with average performance tiers.

The instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local SSD storage or GPU acceleration. The high memory density relative to the 32 vCPUs makes it suitable for in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, and memory-bound data processing tasks. However, the weak large-block memory bandwidth represents a performance tradeoff for workloads requiring massive sequential memory throughput.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r7a.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs and 256.0 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7T83 processor at 2.55 GHz. Built on the KVM hypervisor, this x86_64 server provides 8.0 GB of memory per core but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities and high PassMark memory scores, contrasted by weaker large-block memory read and write bandwidths. Multi-core processing, database operations, and Redis transaction speeds remain in the average tier. This hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications that prioritize high RAM capacity over local storage speed.
